transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-27
Start time: 16:00 UTC
Scheduled duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Jordan (CSM), Nina (SRE), Samir (MLOps), Laura (VP Eng)

Summary (auto): quick postmortem follow-up after 2026-09-20 production spike. Discussed root causes (batching and KV cache thrash), mitigations (prefix caching + throttles), and path to a controlled pilot on Dedicated capacity. Agreed on data handoff, benchmark run, and security/telemetry docs.

Topics: 1) What happened during spike; 2) immediate mitigations; 3) telemetry gaps and audit logs; 4) pilot scope and success criteria; 5) timelines and owners.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): All right hi everyone, thanks for joining. we wanted to make sure we followed up on last weeks spike. start with a super short recap then hand to Ethan for the deeper bit.
[00:12] Nina (SlateBridge SRE): yeah thanks Maya. to be clear we were seeing a lot of tail latency out to 12s for some requests, CPU on the worker nodes shot up and we had a cascade of retries that amplified load.
[00:25] Ethan (Redwood SE): yep and our initial look shows frequent KV cache evictions. in our logs it looked like prefix cache wasn't sticky and the batching window opened and closed, so effectively you got batch fragmentation.
[00:38] Samir (SlateBridge MLOps): sorry when you say KV cache evictions, is that per model or per tenant? we run multi-tenant on one pool.
[00:46] Ethan (Redwood SE): good q. in this case it's per model-shard but because you're co-locating a few model variants without pinning, eviction noise moved across tenants. i think the root was a mismatch between the kv cache size and the sequence length distribution under the sudden long-context prompts. also some clients burst with small-ish requests but high concurrency which defeats batching.
[01:07] Laura (VP Eng): and we think that coincided with a marketing blast that increased chat sessions? i mean the timing lined up.
[01:12] Nina: yep, marketing pushed a new flow around 15:10 UTC that had a long system prompt on first turn.
[01:18] Maya: ok so that's the signal. quick question — were there any regen loops from client side, retries firing?
[01:24] Nina: yes some of our old retry middleware retried on 5xx and that made the traffic shape worse, we removed it yesterday from prod.
[01:31] Ethan: makes sense. couple of mitigation patterns we talked about in the incident doc: 1) enable prefix caching on hot routes, 2) throttle burst QPS at the edge, 3) optionally run a dedicated pool for the busiest model variants to avoid eviction thrash.
[01:46] Samir: dedicated pool sounds good but cost is a big concern — we need predictable unit economics.
[01:51] Jordan (CSM): we've modelled cost tradeoffs; in some workloads Dedicated actually saves money if it prevents repeated long tails and retries.
[02:00] Nina: question on telemetry — during the spike we had sparse traces, some missing request ids. is that something on your side or ours?
[02:08] Ethan: we saw gaps where traces didn't correlate to token-level timelines, often because our SDK didn't surface the upstream request-id header consistently for older clients.
[02:18] Maya: action: we'll share an updated SDK snippet and a trace enrichment guide.
[02:23] Samir: also, audit logs — our security team needs assurance on data retention and who can see payloads.
[02:30] Maya: understood. we have SOC2-II artifacts and KMS rotation docs, i'll attach the redwood security pack.
[02:37] Nina: also can you confirm whether you persist raw prompts in any logs? we need to know what gets redacted.
[02:42] Maya: short answer no, raw prompts are redacted by default in hosted mode, you can opt into richer logs for a dedicated pilot but it's gated by contract.
[02:51] Laura: i'd like a quick matrix: what telemetry we get in hosted vs dedicated vs private.
[02:56] Ethan: we'll make a table, on hosted you'll get aggregate latency histograms, token-level counts, request metadata; on Dedicated you get optional raw request logs and deeper tracing hooks; Private gives full control but you manage storage. note, private also has different support SLAs.
[03:15] Unknown (muffled): [crosstalk]...
[03:20] Maya: ok let's pivot to the pilot scope. recommended pilot: a 2-week burst simulation in staging that mirrors observed marketing pattern, plus a 72-hour pilot on Dedicated with limited tenancy and a rollback window. success criteria — p95 latency under 800ms for 90% of requests during the simulated burst, zero amplification from retries, and no KV eviction rate above threshold.
[03:44] Samir: can we instrument eviction rate? what's that threshold?
[03:48] Ethan: yes we emit eviction_count per minute per shard. threshold we propose is <0.5% of requests causing evictions over a minute, but that's tunable.
[03:58] Nina: we'll need the metric name and a sample query to add to our dashboards.
[04:02] Ethan: will send the metric name (redwood.kv.evictions) and a promql example.
[04:08] Laura: timeline wise, if we get logs by Friday and a staging ramp script by Monday, we could run the staging tests next Wednesday then cut the dedicated pilot the week after.
[04:20] Maya: that sounds realistic. remember to anonymize the payloads when you send them.
[04:24] Nina: yep. also, small thing — we noticed a config form on the console called "batching aggressiveness" that used confusing units. can you clarify?
[04:33] Jordan (CSM): that UI is being overhauled, we can share a sneak peek of the new console copy.
[04:39] Samir: another risk — model version pinning. if a rollout occurs during a pilot we could see changes. can we lock a model sha?
[04:46] Ethan: you can pin model versions per route, and we recommend doing that for pilot. we'll include instructions in the pilot runbook.
[04:54] Nina: on security signoffs — the compliance folks will need an architecture diagram for the dedicated pool and assurance on egress rules.
[05:02] Maya: we'll provide a network diagram and sample VPC config. if you want an on-prem package that's a separate sales path.
[05:09] Laura: are there any quick mitigations we can do before the pilot that don't require a dedicated pool?
[05:15] Ethan: yes: prefix caching, soft throttles at 95th percentile, increase KV cache memory on current nodes, and patch the clients to remove aggressive retries. these are low-effort.
[05:26] Nina: we'll do prefix caching and disable retries this week.
[05:30] Maya: brilliant. any blockers on your side for sharing the ramp script?
[05:33] Nina: no blockers, just need an example of the user journey to simulate.
[05:37] Maya: we'll attach a high-level user flow and an example JMeter script in the follow-up.
[05:43] Samir: on the cost question — can you give us an estimate for a 72-hour Dedicated pilot?
[05:48] Jordan (CSM): we can run estimates; i'll push a spreadsheet today with a best-case/worst-case and cost per token assumptions.
[05:55] Laura: perfect. last thing — regression detection. we need an automated alert if p95 doubles vs baseline during business hours.
[06:02] Ethan: we'll add an alert rule recommendation and sample thresholds.
[06:07] Maya: ok let's recap next steps quickly.
[06:10] Maya: Redwood will: 1) share sanitized logs and escalation doc by 2026-10-01; 2) provide promql and metric names and SDK snippet by 2026-10-01; 3) hand over pilot runbook and model-pinning instructions by 2026-10-05.
[06:25] Nina: SlateBridge will: 1) send anonymized payloads and ramp script by 2026-10-03; 2) disable retry middleware and update dashboards to track evictions by 2026-10-02; 3) review cost spreadsheet and confirm go/no-go for dedicated pilot by 2026-10-07.
[06:44] Samir: can we also schedule the benchmark window for 2026-10-06 14:00 UTC?
[06:49] Maya: scheduled — i'll send a calendar invite after the call.
[06:53] Laura: thanks everyone, appreciate the quick turnaround.
[06:56] Maya: thanks all, we'll follow up in writing.

References and artifacts shared: security pack (link: https://redwood.example.com/safety/slatebridge-security-pack.pdf), incident doc (link: https://redwood.example.com/incidents/2026-09-20-slatebridge-spike.md), pilot runbook stub (drive: https://drive.example.com/s/sb-pilot-runbook).
